display_name: National Insurance Law ss 342 and 348 and Schedule K: who is liable to pay insurance contributions and the employer's deduction from the wage; the maximum, minimum and disregarded income; and the income bounds per month, quarter and year for each kind of insured person

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

depends_on.how: Not imported: the l4 binary resolves an IMPORT by bare module name beside the importing file, so IL-04's modules in the sibling directory are not found (NOTES.md section 8). IL-04's types A branch of insurance and A column of insured persons in Schedule J are declared again with the same names and constructors; IL-04's Schedule J column D amounts and s 334(a) threshold enter as inputs; IL-04's s 337 takes this row's s 348 result as its income input. NOTES.md section 6 lists what to join at IL-07. Version 0.4.0: the s 342(c), (d) and (e1) rules that take the wage take Schedule J column D as functions of an income instead (IL-04's column D deduction on an income), and apply them to the wage as s 348(a) takes it into account.

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). Hebrew is quoted only in `-- src:N |` comments generated mechanically from line N of the deposited source by row IL-04's tools/srcquote.py (run by path, not copied), and in short runs that IL-04's tools/hebcheck.py checks occur verbatim in it.

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval

published_figures.note: Figures the Law computes but does not print, taken from the National Insurance Institute's pages fetched 2026-10-06; URLs and sha256 in nii-il05-published-figures.l4 and NOTES.md section 7.

scope: Encoded: s 342(a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2) (pension, age, police and prison officers, the employer's permission to reduce), (d) with its two definitions, (e1), (f)(1)-(2); s 348(a), (a1), (b), (c) (the power's test, and a decline where an order reaches), (d) (where its readings agree), (e) permanent and temporary texts; Schedule K in full, four items, maximum and minimum, per month, quarter and year, with 'quarter', 'minimum wage' and 'basic amount'. Inert: headings; s 342(e)(1)-(4) and (f)(3), powers whose regulations are not in the sources. Out of scope: Schedule K1 (only s 369 refers to it), and every provision outside the slice, each taken as an input with its citation (NOTES.md section 2). Version 0.4.0: s 342(c), (d) and (e1) also on a wage, with s 348(a) applied inside them (05-RC2); s 342(a)-(b) for one who is both employee and self-employed in one call (05-P3).

years_answered.contribution periods: January 2026 on; earlier periods declined by name (s 342's text is from 1 January 2026 by the 2025 budget-year Law s 19(4) and s 21; this row answers with row IL-04)
years_answered.figures: 2026 from the Institute's published figures; 2027 on only when the caller supplies them
years_answered.s 348(e) temporary text: to 31.8.2026, and after it for one who began national-civic service before that day

Findings about the source, not defects of the encoding: NOTES.md section 0, forks F10 and F22.

The independent tester's module. At 0.1.0 and 0.3.0: 15 failed and 2 refused. NOTES.md 'Version 0.4.0'. Version 0.6.0 (SHRUG, BACKLOG IL-50): four assertions declined at the new switch (lines 367 and 371, G3 and G5, 05-X1; 395 and 396, H6, 05-F6) were re-pointed by the lead, with the lead's yes and on the ADDENDUM terms, to the readings the tester decided, by name, values unchanged; they pass, and the counts are as at 0.5.0.

forks.F1: Schedule K and s 348(a1) read the average wage calculated under s 2 (13,769 for 2026): s 2(b) applies 'for benefits and contributions', and every Institute figure checked fits it and not the s 1 figure. (0.6.0) Row IL-04's 04-F5, this row's side: class (b) under SHRUG, the only reading the text supports for contributions (s 2(b), line 236); input convention: the figures record names its average wage.
forks.F2: Items 2-4 print no monthly figure; a month's is a third of the quarter's.
forks.F3: s 348(a1) is a deduction of up to 25% of the average wage, not all-or-nothing (the other reading is encoded beside it). (0.4.0, 05-X1/P1) Reason restated: not 'the same construction from below' as (a), which it is not (line 3763 'the amount' with יבוא; line 3764 'the income' with תובא and a qualifying clause); the words read at least as naturally as all or nothing, and the deduction is taken because the Institute's published example applies it. Answer unchanged. (0.6.0) Ruled by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG), 05-X1: a switch (`A reading of section 348(a1)`), declined by default where the deduction and all-or-nothing give different answers, both kept by name and tested.
forks.F4: s 348(a1)'s sum is a month's; other periods with income not from work are declined.
forks.F5: s 348(d) as a deeming or a floor: answered only where both agree (income not above the item 3 minimum). (0.6.0) 05-RC4, class (b) under SHRUG: already declined where deeming and floor differ, and a quarter is declined.
forks.F6: Schedule K item 3 is the classes s 348(d) and (e) name, whatever their income. (0.6.0) Ruled by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG), 05-F6: a switch (`A reading of Schedule K item 3's "as stated in section 348(d) and (e)"`): the classes, or one of (e)'s classes only while (e)'s income condition holds; declined by default where they differ, both kept by name and tested.
forks.F7: An employee or self-employed person also in a (d) or (e) class keeps item 1 or 2; where (d) or (e) would then disagree with (b), declined. (0.6.0) Ruled by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG), 05-F6: a switch (`A reading of the Schedule K item of an employee or a self-employed person of a class section 348(d) or (e) names`): item 1 or 2 by status, or item 3 by the class; declined by default where they differ, both kept by name and tested.
forks.F8: s 348(e)'s temporary text ends 31.8.2026; 'began before' is strict; a quarter or year across the date, for one who began on or after it, is declined. (0.6.0) 05-Q7, class (d) under SHRUG: whether the date moved after Amendment 9 needs a source not held here; the National-Civic Service Law is now deposited (commons 317b20c5) and BACKLOG IL-34 is to encode it.
forks.F9: s 342(c)(2): a month in which the age is reached after its first day, or the pension is payable for part of it, is declined. (0.6.0) 05-F9, class (b) under SHRUG: already declined where apportioning and the whole month differ.
forks.F10: s 342(c)(2)'s 'subject to s 245(b2)' has no effect: s 245(b2) is repealed (checked red).
forks.F11: Schedule K's minimum wage is the particular employee's (an input); for an employee with none given, item 1's minimum is declined.
forks.F12: s 342(c)(1)'s s 335 subsections are the branches maternity, accident injury, unemployment, disability, long-term care, senior citizens and survivors.
forks.F13: A deduction branch with no column D amount in the case is declined, not taken as 0.
forks.F14: The coordinated contributions of s 342(d) are s 342(c), (c)(2) included, on the total income as one employer's wage.
forks.F15: s 342(e1) when the other employer deducted more than the coordinated contributions: declined.
forks.F16: s 342(f)(2)'s 'lower than' is strict (nothing turns on it).
forks.F17: Whether s 348(b)'s minimum applies per employer or to the total under s 342(b): not modelled.
forks.F18: s 350(c) disapplies s 348(b) only, not (d) or (e).
forks.F19: The day an age is reached: the date of birth plus the months, keeping the day or the month's last day. (0.4.0) A day the shorter month lacks is fork DATE. (0.5.0) Kept by name as fork DATE's reading 'the last day of that month'; no longer the default.
forks.F20: Schedule K's yearly figures are for a whole tax year; part years are not modelled.
forks.F21: 'the deduction in item 6 of Schedule J' is the unemployment branch's column D amount.
forks.F22: s 342(e)(3)-(4)'s 'column E' for deduction rates is not resolved (checked red; (e) decides nothing here).
forks.F23: (0.3.0) At the printed totals of Schedule J (row IL-04's fork F4, ruled 2026-10-07), a police or prison officer's deduction leaves out 'the deduction in item 6' as item 6's own amount: the total for the deduction branches together less the unemployment branch's amount. (0.6.0) Row IL-04's 04-Q2, this row's side: class (b) under SHRUG; it gives row IL-04's fork F21 default for the same branch set (TAKEAWAY).
forks.F24: (0.3.0) Row IL-04's fork F4, ruled 2026-10-07: s 342(c)(1)'s 'as in Schedule J' is read at the printed totals by default, an amount for the branches in which the employer deducts together that the caller gives as an argument (row IL-04's column D deduction at its default reading), the items' reading (the per-branch amounts summed) kept as the alternative. One switch: `section 342(c) — the reading of Schedule J this row takes where its totals row and its items differ`. The rules under their 0.1.0 names read the items.
forks.F25: (0.4.0, assumed by the repair agent, not ruled) The s 342(c), (d) and (e1) rules that take the wage apply s 348(a) to it (the wage, or the Schedule K item 1 maximum for a month if lower) and not s 348(b)'s minimum, which with several employers is fork F17 (not modelled); a caller who applies (b) gives the minimum as the wage. The capstone's fork K8 (i) applies both.
forks.DATE: (0.5.0) Ruled by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG): one switch, `section 342(c)(2) — the reading this row takes of a day of birth the month of the age lacks`, default `such a day is declined` (refusal: 'section 342(c)(2) does not say on what day the insured reaches the age when the month it falls in lacks the day of the month of birth'); `the last day of that month` (the clamp, this row's reading before 0.5.0) and `the first day of the next month` kept by name and tested. (0.4.0 record) Readings: (i) clamp, held by this row's encoder (F19), IL-06's (F2) and IL-08's (N4); (ii) roll, held by no one; (iii) decline, held by the independent testers of IL-06 and IL-08 and recommended by the lead.
forks.F26: (0.5.0, assumed by the agent, not ruled) Fork DATE's decline declines only the month in which its other two readings answer differently (the month the age falls in, with no senior citizen pension for any of it), and answers every other month as both do; the day rule itself declines.
